Important note: Always look to see if there is compression directly above/below an entry. If there is compression, always be sure to place SL just beyond it. If trading conservatively, place the limit order right at the PCP edge for the highest RR.

author: hoeschec
text:
In reference to my post # 1937:

It is always hard to decide whether a lost trade is simply a fluke of the market (which happens) or if it was an error on my part. Post # 1937 is a perfect example. At first, I wrote it off as a 'fluke'. but after seeing the perfect reaction on the EA trade on post # 1938, I think I am still missing a piece of critical analysis.

My hunch is that the 'missing piece' has everything to do with the relationship between a swap zone & a FO. It is important to see where the FO occurs... I remember Salivan mentioning something about looking for a FO that occurs in to another FL. He might mean that the FO needs to dip through the FL in to the opposite swap zone to clear out all residual LQ.

If you refer back to my EUR-AUD trade on Post # 1938, you will see a great entry point with very little DD. If you look to the left of my entry, you will see a clear FO that occurs below the distal edge of the black box. That FO and subsequent high is drawn using the blue box. I am pretty sure the false move to the downside (in to a PAZ below) is key in getting the right bounce when price returns for the FOF that remains at that level.

My apologies if I am doing a bad job of explaining this... there concepts are notoriously difficult to describe using words

But for those who are struggling....start looking left and spend more time understanding what price is doing as it forms prior to the main FL where you start looking for an entry. Left side data is crucial, and I am still learning how to read it properly.

Confluence of the following factors is important as well:

1. Swap Zone

2. FO/False moves 3. Clean orders 4. Squaring up 5. Drawing FL Boxes & decisions in the right FL to prepare for an entry 6. ** False supply/demand zones that set up just above/below true supply or true demand. 5. Opposing targets (aka opposing tricks)

This is what I will continue working on.

Here is a simple version of the EA trade that worked out well in my post above.

If you look at the chart below, you will see I labeled FL "A" for reference. There is a tiny LTF kink that forms after price breaks the top of FL "A", but price forms a FO below that kink as well. The FO drops all the way back in to FL "A" (imagine if I extended FL "A" all the way to the right...). I think this holds importance because it is clearing residual LQ, making it much more likely that price will bounce bullish when price RT to the yellow box I drew.

We always want to make sure the last pocket of short orders is taken if we are looking to get long, otherwise, price is likely to do whatever is necessary to absorb that LQ. Clearing the last pocket of sell orders loads the buyers, and we can proceed to mark up the correct FL to find where the opposite orders are executed and FOF is created. [/b]

Hey buddy,

I use FXCM free simulation software. Just sign up for a Demo account (free) with FXCM and it is included. It is not the best performing simulation program (it freezes all the time...but it is free!)

Here is a link to FXCM's page to sign up for a demo account.

www.fxcm.com/uk/forex-trading-demo/

Once you login to the demo platform, look at the menu and choose:

System, Simulation Mode, New

Then, it will ask you to confirm logging out of the demo platform and it will automatically log you in to a 'simulation session' where you can choose a pair/time frame/account balance, leverage, etc...

From that point on it is pretty intuitive.

One warning: Once you start 'playing' the simulation forward, do not click anywhere on the chart unless you pause the simulation first. If you do, it will freeze up and you will have to restart.

Let me know if you have any issues with it and I am happy to help. It is a great resource that has helped me tremendously.

Good luck!

text:
Mukhcin wrote: and one more last question H, i can't find if there is any way of making pending orders in simulation tests. or only market orders? thanks in advance

Yes, you can.

Just right click on the chart where you want to place your order and choose "entry order". Then you can set up the SL and TG.

Another quirk: if you want to adjust the SL or TG after originally placing your order, you can do it. Just make sure you pause the simulation first. Important: you can't change the entry order once you place it (super frustrating). If you want to adjust your entry order, you need to cancel the entire order and start over.

Hope that helps!
